title: Genetic mosaic dissection of candidate genes in mice using mosaic analysis with double markers
protocol: Cross MADMTG/TG animals with a mouse line mutant for gene-X.
The resulting F1 generation will be trans-heterozygous for the MADM TG cassette and the mutation of interest (genotype will be MADMTG/+; gene-X+/-).
Cross MADMGT/GT animals with a Cre driver of choice.
Allow the resulting F1 generation to grow up to 8 weeks of age.
For breeding strategy 2, proceed to step 6.
For breeding strategy 1, cross MADMTG/+; gene-X+/- mice with MADMTG/TG animals to generate F2 offspring homozygous for the MADM TG cassette and meiotically linked gene-X.
For breeding strategy 1, intercross MADMGT/+; Cre+/- mice with MADMGT/+; Cre+/- animals in order to generate F2 offspring homozygous for the MADM GT cassette and the Cre driver.
Allow the resulting F2 generation from both steps to grow up to 8 weeks of age.
Cross MADMTG/TG,gene-X mice with MADMGT/GT; Cre+/+ animals to generate experimental offspring.
Monitor successful mating by checking for the vaginal plug.
Use male and female offspring as experimental animals.
Perform experiments at the desired developmental stage.
Cross trans-heterozygous MADMTG/+;gene-X+/- mice directly with double heterozygous MADMGT/+; Cre+/- animals to generate experimental MADM offspring.
Monitor successful mating by checking for the vaginal plug.
Use male and female offspring as experimental animals.
Perform experiments at developmental stages of choice.
Cross MADMGT/GT; Emx1Cre/Cre or MADMGT/GT; Nestin-Cre+/+ females with MADMTG/TG;gene-X males to generate offspring for population analysis.
Monitor successful mating by checking for the vaginal plug.
Use F1 generation offspring as experimental animals.
Perform experiment at your desired postnatal time point.
Ensure generation of cell types is completed.
Confirm cells have reached a fully developed, mature state.
Cross MADMGT/GT; HprtCre/+ females with MADMTG/TG,gene-X males to generate offspring with genetic mosaic tissues.
Monitor for vaginal plugs to check successful mating and facilitate experimental planning.
Use males of the resulting F1 generation as experimental animals (genotype will be MADMGT/TG,gene-X; HprtCre/+).
Perform color swap and parent swap if desired, as described in the protocol notes.
Perform the experiment at the desired postnatal time point.
Anesthetize the animal by intraperitoneal injection of anesthesia working solution at a volume of 0.16–0.24 mL/10 g mouse (equivalent to 400–600 mg/kg).
Test the efficiency of anesthesia by pinching a paw with forceps.
Proceed with dissection and perfusion only when the mouse does not display any movement after pinching.
Place the anesthetized animal in a supine position on a perfusion tray.
Disinfect the fur with 70% ethanol.
Make a medial incision below the rib cage through the skin and underlying muscle layer.
Continue cutting laterally along the incision.
Lift the tip of the sternum and snip the diaphragm.
Trim the rib cage to expose the heart.
Make an incision at the posterior end of the right atrium for blood drainage.
Insert a needle attached to a peristaltic pump or syringe filled with 1× PBS into the lower left ventricle.
Perfuse with PBS until the liver turns pale (approximately 5–10 mL).
Switch the perfusion solution to 4% PFA.
Perfuse pups manually using 10 mL syringes.
Prepare two distinct 10 mL syringes: one filled with 1× PBS and another with 4% PFA.
Replace the PBS-containing syringe plus needle with fresh needle and syringe containing PFA through the same puncture hole in the heart after perfusion completion.
Perfuse juvenile and adult mice using a peristaltic pump.
Place one end of the tube of the peristaltic pump into a flask or Falcon tube filled with PBS.
Switch to 4% PFA by briefly stopping the peristaltic pump and exchanging the PBS solution with ice-cold 4% PFA after perfusion with PBS.
Resume perfusion with PFA at the same speed as before.
Remove mouse from perfusion pad.
Dissect the organ of interest.
Decapitate mouse if brain is the organ of interest.
Remove skin over the skull.
Cut skull at the naso-frontal suture in front of the olfactory bulbs.
Cut along the midline.
Follow with a cut along the parietal-interparietal sutures.
Lift the skull to the side to expose the brain.
Place curved forceps or a thin spatula underneath the brain and remove it from the skull.
Transfer the brain to a well filled with ice-cold 4% PFA in a 6-well plate.
Incubate at 4°C for a minimum of 10 hours.
Wash three times with 1× PBS for 5 minutes each.
Transfer the brain to a 15 mL Falcon tube filled with 10 mL of 30% Sucrose.
Incubate at 4°C until the brain has sunk to the bottom of the Falcon tube.
Remove the brain from sucrose and gently remove residual sugar from the surface using lint-free tissues.
Place the brain ventral-side down on a piece of lint-free tissue for coronal orientation.
Remove the cerebellum using a razor blade.
Place the brain with the caudal side down in an embedding mold.
Fill the mold and cover the tissue with O.C.T. Tissue Tek.
Freeze the embedded brain.
Store the frozen brain at −80°C.
Place brain ventral-side down on a piece of lint-free tissue.
Cut brain in two halves along the midline using a razor blade.
Place one half of the brain with the medial side down in an embedding mold.
Fill the embedding mold and cover the tissue with O.C.T. Tissue Tek.
Freeze the tissue.
Store the frozen tissue at -80°C.
Remove colon from the mouse and place it on lint-free tissue.
Cut open the colon longitudinally.
Remove faeces from the colon.
Roll the colon into a Swiss roll using a pipet tip.
Transfer the rolled colon into a histosette.
Incubate the colon in a beaker filled with 4% PFA for 4 hours at 22°C–25°C.
Wash the colon 3 times with 1× PBS for 5 minutes each.
Incubate the colon in 30% Sucrose at 4°C for a minimum of 10 hours.
Remove the histosette with the colon from sucrose.
Take out the colon and gently remove residual sugar from its surface using lint-free tissues.
Transfer the colon to an embedding mold, fill the mold and cover the tissue with O.C.T. Tissue Tek.
Freeze the colon.
Store the frozen colon at -80°C.
Pause point: Keep the frozen tissue at −80°C until further usage.
Place embedding molds on dry ice for optimal tissue freezing during embedding.
Control the tissue during the freezing process from time to time and avoid loss of position within the mold.
Remove tissue from −80°C and transfer to a cryostat cooled to −20°C.
Let tissue adapt to temperature change for 20 min.
Remove tissue block from the embedding mold.
Attach the tissue block to the specimen disk in the cryostat by applying a drop of OCT to the disk and placing the tissue block directly into the OCT.
Allow to freeze for 1–2 min.
Insert disk with attached tissue block in the sectioning holder by placing the tissue in a correct orientation.
Start cutting by trimming the tissue block in 45 μm thick sections until the region of interest is reached.
Slice the tissue in 30 μm thick sections.
Either collect the slices in individual wells of a 24 well plate (= floating sections) or mount them directly onto frosted glass slides.
Fill a Petri dish with PBS-T.
Place a frosted glass slide at the edge of the petri dish so that it is covered up nearly to the label with PBS-T.
Transfer all desired sections into the dish filled with PBS-T.
Use a small paint brush to maneuver the sections onto the slide and arrange them side by side.
Horizontally transfer the slide to a dark slide chamber and let the sections dry completely (∼15 min) to make them adhere to the glass.
Rehydrate and wash sections 3× 5 min with 1× PBS.
Incubate sections with 1 mL pre-heated citrate buffer pH 6.0 for 25 min at 85°C in a dark and closed staining chamber.
Remove the staining chamber and let chill on bench for 15 min.
Open the staining chamber slightly to cool down samples efficiently.
Wash sections 3× 5 min with 1× PBS.
Incubate sections with 500 μL Blocking Solution for 1 h.
Place humidified tissues into the staining chamber.
Dilute primary antibodies in Staining Solution.
Add 250 μL antibody mix for one sample and incubate 8–12 hours at 4°C.
Wash 3× 5 minutes with 1× PBS.
Dilute secondary antibodies in Staining Solution.
Add 250 μL antibody mix for one sample and incubate for 2 hours.
Wash 3× 5 minutes with 1× PBS.
Add 1 mL DAPI working solution for 15 minutes.
Wash 1× 10 minutes in PBS.
Embed the slides with Mowiol and let dry at 22°C–25°C for 30 minutes.
Select the correct laser lines and filters for MADM tissue analysis using an inverted confocal microscope, such as Zeiss LSM800.
Choose excitation wavelengths of 405 nm (for DAPI), 488 nm (for FITC / GFP), 561 nm (for Alexa568 / tdT), and 640 nm (for Alexa647) for imaging.
Set pinhole to 1 airy unit for optimal imaging quality.
Select functions “Z-stack” and “Tiles” from the acquisition dashboard.
Choose objective, scanning speed, resolution, and averaging appropriate for your experiments.
Adjust laser intensity and gain for each channel.
Identify area of interest and set position and imaging tiles to cover it.
Adjust z-stack to capture all MADM-labeled cells in tissue.
Assign center position of Z-stack to tiles and initiate image acquisition by clicking “Start”.
Save the image in .czi file format.
For tissue overview images and cell number quantification, select a 10× objective and use a scanning speed pixel dwell value of 1.52–2.06 μs with resolution 1024 × 1024 and no averaging.

For high-quality images and morphological analysis, use a high magnification objective (e.g., 63×) and use a scanning speed pixel dwell value up to 2.06 μs with resolution 1024 × 1024 and 2× or 4× averaging.
Once image acquisition is completed, use the image processing dashboard in ZEN blue.
Perform maximum intensity projection using the “Orthogonal Projection” function.
Perform “Stitching” function by fusing tiles.
Save the projected and stitched image as a new .czi file.
Export the projected and stitched .czi file to TIFF format.
Export DAPI channel individually for subsequent image analysis.
Export GFP channel individually for subsequent image analysis.
Export tdT channel individually for subsequent image analysis.
Export Alexa647 channel individually for subsequent image analysis.
